summary: Erling Haaland is six goals short of Jorgen Juve's Norway scoring record of 33, which has stood since 1934 and is the longest-standing outright national record among FIFA nations. The article compares long-lasting records in Denmark, Hungary and Italy, explains why such records are now rare, and notes Haaland's near goal-a-game rate. It ends by questioning whether Norway will qualify for a major tournament with him.
one_line: Erling Haaland is six goals from breaking Jorgen Juve's 89-year-old Norway scoring record, prompting a look at other long-standing international records.
key_facts: Erling Haaland is six goals away from Norway's international goalscoring record and only scored his first Norway goals in 2020.
Jorgen Juve scored 33 goals in 45 matches for Norway, including five hat-tricks, and ended his international career in 1937.
Juve played as a centre-forward in less than half his games, otherwise in defence, and captained Norway to bronze at the 1936 Olympics; his last goal came in June 1934.
Poul "Tist" Nielsen scored 52 goals in 38 games for Denmark between 1910 and 1925; Jon Dahl Tomasson equalled the record in 2010 and then retired after the World Cup.
Only six countries' goalscoring records have stood for more than 50 years; among World Cup qualifiers only Denmark, Norway and Hungary.
Ferenc Puskas scored 84 goals in 85 games for Hungary; his international career ended at 29 due to the Hungarian Revolution, and he later played for Spain at the 1962 World Cup.
Sixty-four of 211 nations' record goalscorers have appeared for them in 2023, and the median record has stood for just seven years.
Italy's record is Giga Riva's 35 goals, set by World Cup 1974; Roberto Baggio and Alessandro Del Piero reached 27, and Ciro Immobile has 17.
Haaland averages nearly a goal a game for Norway, while Cristiano Ronaldo has 127 for Portugal at 0.63 goals per game.
Norway play the Faroe Islands in a home friendly, then a Euro qualifier against Scotland in Glasgow on Sunday.
Norway have qualified for only four major tournaments (1938, 1994, 1998, 2000) and won a combined three matches in them.
Spain and Scotland have secured the top two spots in Norway's Euro 2024 group, so Norway likely face two must-win play-off games in March.
